_note: The SINGLE definition of 'agent-relevant change' for this repository. The changed-path classifier (scripts/orientation-contract.mjs), the two-way release gate (scripts/check-release-ledger.mjs), the generated reference (docs/orientation-contract-reference.md), and every contract test read this file. Do not hand-maintain a second copy anywhere. Authoring rules and worked pass/fail examples: docs/release-ledger-authoring-guide.md.
definition: A change is agent-relevant when it alters something a downstream agent orients on: hashed or named supported-surface paths, CLI commands/subcommands/flags, skills, schemas, package exports, compatibility policy, agent-facing documentation, repository workflows that produce those artifacts, or the generated runtime a consumer must rebuild. This is the union of the release-gate list and the same-surface list in the harness upgrade build plan; neither list alone is normative.

schema.description: A JSON Schema in schemas/ that a consumer validates artifacts against.

hashed_surface.description: A path recorded in contracts/supported-surface.json hashed{}; its bytes are pinned and a change owes a surface_version advance.

named_surface.description: A path recorded in contracts/supported-surface.json named[]; content may evolve but the path must keep existing.

cli_surface.description: A CLI command, subcommand, or flag reachable from the supported argv surface.

skill.description: A versioned skill package or its installer.

package_export.description: package.json exports, bin, files, engines, or the dependency/script set a consumer installs.

compatibility_policy.description: The published compatibility statement, the supported-surface manifest, or the documents that define surface discipline.

documentation.description: Agent-facing documentation of record: the agent entry point, contract references, and authoring guides.

workflow.description: A repository workflow or workflow contract that produces or gates a supported artifact.

generated_runtime.description: Sources or lockfiles for the generated runtime a consumer must prepare before use.

_evaluation_note: Evaluation order is fixed and total: self_referential_exemptions -> rules -> derived_from_supported_surface -> ignored -> unclassified (an error). First match wins within each ordered list. match.kind is one of exact | prefix. A rule may carry match_suffix (the path must also end with it) and exclude[] (matches that make the rule NOT apply, so a narrower path falls through to a later rule or to ignored). The derived pass runs BEFORE ignored so that a path newly added to the supported surface can never be swallowed by a broad ignore prefix; that is the fail-closed direction.

self_referential_exemptions.reason: The ledger records changes; recording a change in it is not itself a recorded change.
Changelog sections are linked one-to-one from ledger entries and are enforced by the changelog correspondence gate, not by a separate change item.

_ignored_note: Explicitly NOT agent-relevant. Every ignore carries a reason so 'no agent impact' is an asserted classification, not an omission. A changed path that matches no exemption, rule, derived surface entry, or ignore is an error (unclassified_path) — the classifier fails closed.

ignored.reason: Test fixtures. Consumer-facing fixtures reach the supported surface through contracts/supported-surface.json named[], which the derived pass classifies first.
Implementation. Explicitly unsupported except through declared package exports, which package.json changes classify.

Tests, fixtures, and packaging metadata for the generated runtime. The runtime sources a consumer must rebuild are classified by the generated_runtime rule first; only that rule's exclusions reach here.
Architecture decision records: rationale, not a consumed contract.
Documentation that is not on the named supported surface and not an agent document of record. Named docs are classified by the derived pass first.
Repository front page; the agent entry point is AGENTS.md.
Internal build/QA contract data. Supported contract files are classified by explicit rules or the derived pass first.
Repository metadata other than workflows, which an explicit rule classifies first.

derived_from_supported_surface._note: Every path in hashed{} and named[] is agent-relevant by construction. Deriving this instead of copying the list is what keeps a newly declared surface entry from being born unclassified.
